articleMarkdown:
# Learning from After Completion (Jì Jì): look after what has been accomplished

After something is completed, it still needs handover, maintenance, and checks; completion does not mean it will never need attention again.

Jiji literally suggests having crossed or completed. Its alternating yin and yang lines also occupy their traditionally corresponding positions, presenting an ordered figure. Yet the judgment immediately says a favorable beginning can end in disorder, and the final line describes the danger of a wet head. It directs readers to an often overlooked stage: after the goal is reached.

既济 is hexagram 63 in the traditional King Wen sequence, with the symbol ䷾. Its lower trigram is 离☲ and its upper trigram is 坎☵, traditionally associated with fire and water respectively. Count the lines from the bottom: 初九, 六二, 九三, 六四, 九五, 上六. A solid line is yang; a broken line is yin. Nine and six identify yang and yin in the line labels; they do not add extra lines.

Line structure (bottom to top): 1 0 1 0 1 0

Six-line figure, displayed top to bottom; line numbering starts at the bottom.

```text
━━━━ ━━━━  上六
━━━━━━━━━  九五
━━━━ ━━━━  六四
━━━━━━━━━  九三
━━━━ ━━━━  六二
━━━━━━━━━  初九
```

## The judgment

既濟：亨小。利貞。初吉終亂。

Original editorial rendering, not a quotation from Legge: After completion: favorable progress in small matters. Constancy is beneficial. A favorable beginning; disorder at the end.

Legge explains Jiji as the major undertaking accomplished, with smaller matters still requiring attention to consolidate the established order. In his reading, the favorable beginning and disordered ending warn of possible complacency, not a natural law that all success must eventually fail.

For modern study, distinguish delivery, acceptance, everyday use, and later maintenance. A finished result means only that a particular stage has met its conditions. Who takes over, how it is updated, and whom to contact with problems still require clear arrangements.

Sources: [zhouyi-63](https://zh.wikisource.org/w/index.php?title=周易/既濟&oldid=2572417), [legge1882-63](https://tianmu.org/good-work-library/confucian/general-texts/the-i-ching-james-legge)

## Interpretation in the Ten Wings

The Commentary on the Judgment and the Commentary on the Images belong to the Yi Zhuan, the commentaries usually called the “Ten Wings.” Here their explanations are kept distinct from the judgment and line texts, before turning to modern applications for study.

The Commentary on the Judgment explains Jiji through firm and yielding lines in their proper positions and notes disorder if effort stops at the end. The Commentary on the Images depicts water above fire and proposes anticipating problems and preventing them. Prevention here should mean targeted care, not endless speculation about the worst possible outcome.

This article’s ordinary application is to retain necessary records, assign maintenance responsibility, and check known weak points. Real risk judgments come from evidence and applicable standards; a hexagram cannot replace technical, medical, or legal conclusions.

Sources: [zhouyi-63](https://zh.wikisource.org/w/index.php?title=周易/既濟&oldid=2572417), [hon-sep](https://plato.stanford.edu/entries/chinese-change/)

## 初九 · Completion need not be followed by an immediate restart

曳其輪，濡其尾，无咎。

Original editorial rendering, not a quotation from Legge: Holding back the wheel, wetting the tail. No blame.

Holding back the wheel and wetting the tail are read by Legge as slowing fresh advance after success to avoid renewed rashness.

After finishing an event, first organize unresolved matters before deciding whether to expand the next one immediately. A brief pause gives the result a proper conclusion. Continued busyness need not be the only expression of a positive attitude.

Sources: [zhouyi-63](https://zh.wikisource.org/w/index.php?title=周易/既濟&oldid=2572417), [legge1882-63](https://tianmu.org/good-work-library/confucian/general-texts/the-i-ching-james-legge)

## 六二 · A missing part need not prompt panic

婦喪其茀，勿逐，七日得。

Original editorial rendering, not a quotation from Legge: The woman loses her carriage covering. Do not pursue it; in seven days it is regained.

Legge interprets 茀 as a carriage covering. After its loss, one does not pursue it hastily and regains it in seven days. The image retains the ritual conventions of ancient women’s travel.

First establish how the missing item affects the current task and whether a substitute is available. Seven days is not a guaranteed recovery period, nor does it mean that every real problem requiring action can simply be left to wait.

Sources: [zhouyi-63](https://zh.wikisource.org/w/index.php?title=周易/既濟&oldid=2572417), [legge1882-63](https://tianmu.org/good-work-library/confucian/general-texts/the-i-ching-james-legge)

## 九三 · Even a successful undertaking may consume substantial resources

高宗伐鬼方，三年克之，小人勿用。

Original editorial rendering, not a quotation from Legge: Gaozong attacks the Guifang, overcoming them after three years. Do not employ lesser people.

The ancient text mentions Gaozong attacking the Guifang and prevailing only after three years. Legge explains its difficulty through an ancient dynastic war and warns that those entrusted with the task must be suitable. His proposed specific chronology is not established as fact here.

The modern analogy takes only the reminder that major affairs need time, ability, and support. Ancient campaigns cannot authorize present expansion or confrontation, and a hexagram cannot classify others as lesser people unfit for responsibility.

Sources: [zhouyi-63](https://zh.wikisource.org/w/index.php?title=周易/既濟&oldid=2572417), [legge1882-63](https://tianmu.org/good-work-library/confucian/general-texts/the-i-ching-james-legge)

## 六四 · Prepare practical remedies for known weak points

繻有衣袽，終日戒。

Original editorial rendering, not a quotation from Legge: With fine cloth, have rags ready; remain watchful throughout the day. In the interpretation followed here, the rags are for a leaking boat.

The meanings and readings of 繻 and 衣袽 are debated. Legge adopts the explanation of preparing rags against a leaking boat. This article identifies that as the commentary followed, not a complete set of instructions for operating a vessel.

Ordinary work can retain backups, handover records, or alternatives. Preparation should answer genuinely possible problems rather than expand precautions without limit so that no one can ever finish work.

Sources: [zhouyi-63](https://zh.wikisource.org/w/index.php?title=周易/既濟&oldid=2572417), [legge1882-63](https://tianmu.org/good-work-library/confucian/general-texts/the-i-ching-james-legge)

## 九五 · Grand forms may be inferior to timely, sincere action

東鄰殺牛，不如西鄰之禴祭，實受其福。

Original editorial rendering, not a quotation from Legge: The eastern neighbor slaughters an ox, but this is inferior to the western neighbor’s modest yue offering, which truly receives the blessing.

The eastern neighbor’s slaughtered ox is contrasted with the western neighbor’s modest offering. Legge emphasizes sincerity, while the Small Image stresses timing. The text does not encourage continually increasing offerings to purchase an outcome.

After completion, express thanks specifically, promptly, and in proportion to actual contributions. A careful handover or an accurate explanation may care for the result and its participants better than a lavish celebration.

Sources: [zhouyi-63](https://zh.wikisource.org/w/index.php?title=周易/既濟&oldid=2572417), [legge1882-63](https://tianmu.org/good-work-library/confucian/general-texts/the-i-ching-james-legge)

## 上六 · Having crossed is no reason to disregard danger again

濡其首，厲。

Original editorial rendering, not a quotation from Legge: The head is wet. Danger.

From the first line’s wet tail to the top line’s wet head, the severity plainly increases. Legge explains the danger of advancing rashly again and getting in too deep.

Even after becoming familiar with a process, notice whether its conditions have changed. Past smooth progress does not guarantee that the same approach applies now. What needs checking should be determined by specific changes.

Sources: [zhouyi-63](https://zh.wikisource.org/w/index.php?title=周易/既濟&oldid=2572417), [legge1882-63](https://tianmu.org/good-work-library/confucian/general-texts/the-i-ching-james-legge)

## The work after a shared handbook is finished

Original modern scenario

A group finally completes a handbook for newcomers and first asks actual users whether they can follow its steps to find the information needed. The authors remove outdated material and clearly mark questions that still require separate consultation.

At handover, they establish who maintains links, which changes require updates, and how departing members transfer responsibility. After the celebration, the handbook does not become an unchanging file for which no one is responsible.

Learning from Jiji means acknowledging that completion deserves recognition while caring for the conditions of everyday use. Maintenance need not cancel completion; it lets what has already been accomplished remain useful.

## Avoiding misreadings

- Jiji neither guarantees that success has already been achieved nor predicts its inevitable collapse. First verify what is actually complete.

- Seven days, three years, the wet head, and ancient warfare cannot calculate real deadlines, health conditions, or the outcome of conflicts.

## Three exercises

1. Write clear completion criteria for something just finished and confirm that it has actually met them.

2. List maintenance and handover obligations after delivery and name those responsible.

3. Arrange a check of one weak point supported by existing evidence rather than turning prevention into limitless anxiety.

## Related reading

Weiji — Before Completion (hexagram-64): Jiji concerns sustaining what follows completion; Weiji concerns continuing while completion is still ahead. Placed together at the end of the sixty-four hexagrams, they make completion and incompletion changing circumstances that require ongoing judgment, not fixed labels for a life.

When reading Jiji, ask: as we celebrate what has been accomplished, have we also said who will care for it next?
